title: Using det er and det finnes
goal: Choose between det er for identifying or describing and det finnes for existence or availability.

objectives.statement: Choose between det er for identifying or describing and det finnes for existence or availability.

spans.value: Sara and Jonas have arrived in a small town for a weekend trip. Their hotel room is not ready, so they ask the receptionist, Ingrid, about the hotel and the surrounding area.
Velkommen! Det er jeg som heter Ingrid.

blocks.translation: Welcome! I’m Ingrid.

spans.value: Hei. Vi har bestilt et dobbeltrom.

blocks.translation: Hi. We have booked a double room.

spans.value: Ja, det er rom 214. Det er i andre etasje.

blocks.translation: Yes, it’s room 214. It’s on the second floor.

spans.value: Er rommet klart nå?

blocks.translation: Is the room ready now?

spans.value: Nei, dessverre. Det er ikke klart ennå, men det finnes et bagasjerom ved resepsjonen.

blocks.translation: No, unfortunately. It isn’t ready yet, but there is a luggage room by reception.

spans.value: Fint. Finnes det en kafé på hotellet?

blocks.translation: Great. Is there a café at the hotel?

spans.value: Nei, men det finnes en hyggelig kafé på torget. Det er den røde bygningen ved banken.

blocks.translation: No, but there is a pleasant café in the town square. It’s the red building by the bank.

spans.value: Og hva med middag i kveld?

blocks.translation: And what about dinner tonight?

spans.value: Det finnes flere restauranter i sentrum. Den italienske restauranten er populær, men det er ofte fullt der.

blocks.translation: There are several restaurants in the town centre. The Italian restaurant is popular, but it is often full there.

spans.value: Takk. Da setter vi bagasjen her først.

blocks.translation: Thank you. Then we’ll leave our luggage here first.

spans.value: The two expressions do different jobs in this scene. Ingrid uses
det er
when she identifies or describes something:

no.value: Det er rom 214.

en.value: It is room 214.

no.value: Det er i andre etasje.

en.value: It is on the second floor.

no.value: Det er ikke klart ennå.

en.value: It is not ready yet.

spans.value: She uses
det finnes
when she says that something exists or is available:

no.value: Det finnes et bagasjerom ved resepsjonen.

en.value: There is a luggage room by reception.

no.value: Det finnes flere restauranter i sentrum.

en.value: There are several restaurants in the town centre.

spans.value: The central choice is therefore one of meaning:

items.value: to identify something or describe it.
to say that something exists or is available.

spans.value: English often uses
there is
or
there are
for existence. Norwegian can express that meaning with
det finnes
. The form
finnes
is the present tense of
å finnes
, meaning
to exist
or
to be found

sections.title: Identifying and describing with det er

spans.value: Use
det er
when you tell someone what a person or thing is, or when you give information about it.
Identifying something

no.value: Det er hotellet vårt.

en.value: That is our hotel.

no.value: Det er resepsjonisten.

en.value: That is the receptionist.

no.value: Det er rom 214.

en.value: It is room 214.

no.value: Det er nøkkelen din.

en.value: That is your key.

spans.value: In each example, the speaker points out or identifies a particular person or thing. The meaning is not simply that a hotel, receptionist, room, or key exists. The speaker tells us which person or thing we are looking at or talking about.
Compare:

no.value: Det er hotellet vårt.

en.value: That is our hotel.

no.value: Det finnes et hotell ved stasjonen.

en.value: There is a hotel by the station.

spans.value: The first sentence identifies a particular building as
our hotel
. The second tells us that a hotel exists in a particular place.
Describing something
Once a person, place, or thing is part of the conversation,
det er
can describe it.

no.value: Det er stort.

en.value: It is large.

no.value: Det er ganske dyrt.

en.value: It is quite expensive.

no.value: Det er åpent hele natten.

en.value: It is open all night.

no.value: Det er nær sentrum.

en.value: It is near the town centre.

spans.value: The surrounding context tells us what
det
refers to. For example:

no.value: Hvordan er rommet? Det er lyst og stille.

en.value: What is the room like? It is bright and quiet.

no.value: Hvor er frokostsalen? Det er i første etasje.

en.value: Where is the breakfast room? It is on the first floor.

spans.value: The thing is already known:
the room
or
the breakfast room
. The answer supplies a description or location.

sections.title: Existence and availability with det finnes

spans.value: Use
det finnes
when the important information is that something exists, can be found, or is available.

no.value: Det finnes en kafé på torget.

en.value: There is a café in the town square.

no.value: Det finnes et kart i resepsjonen.

en.value: There is a map at reception.

no.value: Det finnes mange fine turstier i området.

en.value: There are many pleasant hiking trails in the area.

no.value: Det finnes gratis parkering bak hotellet.

en.value: There is free parking behind the hotel.

spans.value: These sentences introduce useful information. The café, map, paths, and parking have not necessarily been mentioned before. The speaker announces their existence or availability.
The same form works with one thing and with several things:

no.value: Det finnes en restaurant i nærheten.

en.value: There is a restaurant nearby.

no.value: Det finnes tre restauranter i nærheten.

en.value: There are three restaurants nearby.

spans.value: Norwegian does not change
finnes
according to whether the following noun is singular or plural. English changes between
there is
and
there are
, but Norwegian keeps
det finnes
Availability is a common reason to use the expression:

no.value: Det finnes ledige rom i helgen.

en.value: There are rooms available this weekend.

no.value: Det finnes kaffe i frokostsalen.

en.value: There is coffee in the breakfast room.

no.value: Det finnes ikke flere billetter.

en.value: There are no more tickets available.

spans.value: The negative form
det finnes ikke
says that something does not exist or is not available.

no.value: Det finnes ikke en minibank på hotellet.

en.value: There is no cash machine at the hotel.

no.value: Det finnes ikke ledige bord akkurat nå.

en.value: There are no tables available right now.

spans.value: To ask whether something exists or is available, place
finnes
before
det

no.value: Finnes det en kafé på hotellet?

en.value: Is there a café at the hotel?

no.value: Finnes det ledige rom i kveld?

en.value: Are there rooms available tonight?

no.value: Finnes det en buss til sentrum?

en.value: Is there a bus to the town centre?

spans.value: The question asks about existence or availability. It does not ask for a description of a known café, room, or bus.
Compare:

no.value: Finnes det en restaurant på hotellet?

en.value: Is there a restaurant at the hotel?

no.value: Er restauranten åpen?

en.value: Is the restaurant open?

spans.value: The first question establishes whether a restaurant exists. The second asks for information about a restaurant that is already known.

sections.title: The same place, two different messages

spans.value: A location phrase does not decide the form by itself. Both expressions can occur with a location, but the speaker’s purpose differs.

no.value: Det finnes en kafé på torget.

en.value: There is a café in the town square.

no.value: Det er den røde bygningen på torget.

en.value: It is the red building in the town square.

spans.value: The first sentence announces that a café exists. The second identifies which building the café is.
Another pair:

no.value: Det finnes et bagasjerom ved resepsjonen.

en.value: There is a luggage room by reception.

no.value: Det er ved resepsjonen.

en.value: It is by reception.

spans.value: In the first sentence, the luggage room is new information. In the second, the listener already knows that there is a luggage room and asks where it is.
Consider a short exchange:
Finnes det et apotek i nærheten?

blocks.translation: Is there a pharmacy nearby?

spans.value: Ja, det finnes et apotek ved busstasjonen.

blocks.translation: Yes, there is a pharmacy by the bus station.

spans.value: Hvilken bygning er det?

blocks.translation: Which building is it?

spans.value: Det er den gule bygningen ved siden av bakeriet.

blocks.translation: It is the yellow building next to the bakery.

spans.value: First Ingrid confirms existence. Then she identifies the building. The physical place has not changed, but the communicative job has.
Compact rule
Ask what the sentence contributes:

items.value: what or which thing it is
what that known thing is like
that something exists or is available

spans.value: It is tempting to translate English word by word:

no.value: Det er en kafé på torget.

en.value: There is a café in the town square.

spans.value: Sentences of this kind can be heard in everyday Norwegian. However,
det er
has several uses, and relying on it for every English
there is
can hide the distinction this lesson is teaching.
When your clear purpose is to say that something exists or is available,
det finnes
makes that meaning explicit:

no.value: Det finnes en kafé på torget.

en.value: There is a café in the town square.

spans.value: When you identify or describe a known thing, use
det er

no.value: Det er kafeen vi leter etter.

en.value: It is the café we are looking for.

no.value: Det er veldig hyggelig der.

en.value: It is very pleasant there.

spans.value: The useful learner strategy is not “translate
there
as
det
.” Instead, decide whether you are announcing existence or giving information about something already in the conversation.
Using det finnes to describe a known thing
Avoid:

no.value: Rommet finnes stort og lyst.

en.value: The room is large and bright. (in this situation)

spans.value: Here, the sentence describes the room. Use
det er

no.value: Rommet er stort og lyst. Det er også stille.

en.value: The room is large and bright. It is also quiet.

spans.value: Finnes
does not work as a substitute for every form of English
is
or
are
Using det er when the task is specifically to express availability
If a guest wants to know whether rooms are available, the intended meaning is existence or availability:

no.value: Finnes det ledige rom i helgen?

en.value: Are there rooms available this weekend?

spans.value: A question such as
Er rommet ledig?
has a different context: it asks whether one particular, already identified room is available.

no.value: Finnes det ledige rom?

en.value: Are there any rooms available?

no.value: Er rommet ledig?

en.value: Is the room available?

spans.value: The first asks whether any suitable rooms exist. The second asks about a specific room.
Changing finnes for a plural noun
Do not create a separate plural form after
det
. Keep
finnes

no.value: Det finnes ett ledig rom.

en.value: There is one room available.

no.value: Det finnes fem ledige rom.

en.value: There are five rooms available.

spans.value: Sara and Jonas come back to reception later that afternoon.
Nå er vi tilbake. Er rommet klart?

blocks.translation: Now we’re back. Is the room ready?

spans.value: Ja, det er klart. Her er nøkkelen.

blocks.translation: Yes, it is ready. Here is the key.

spans.value: Takk. Finnes det håndklær på rommet?

blocks.translation: Thank you. Are there towels in the room?

spans.value: Ja, det finnes håndklær på badet.

blocks.translation: Yes, there are towels in the bathroom.

spans.value: Og internett?

blocks.translation: And internet?

spans.value: Det finnes gratis trådløst internett på hele hotellet. Passordet står på nøkkelkortet.

blocks.translation: There is free Wi-Fi throughout the hotel. The password is printed on the key card.

spans.value: Er det dette passordet?

blocks.translation: Is it this password?

spans.value: Ja, det er riktig.

blocks.translation: Yes, it is correct.

spans.value: The dialogue now moves back and forth between the two meanings:

items.value: announces the availability of a service.
describes the password Jonas has identified.

sections.title: From controlled choice to short connected use

spans.value: Imagine that Jonas sends Sara a message while exploring the hotel. He tells her that a small gym is available downstairs. Then he identifies the door and describes the room.
His message needs to move through three stages:

items.value: Identify which door leads to it.

spans.value: The target forms make that progression clear:

no.value: Det finnes et lite treningsrom i kjelleren.

en.value: There is a small gym in the basement.

no.value: Det er døra ved siden av heisen.

en.value: It is the door next to the lift.

no.value: Det er lyst og ganske moderne.

en.value: It is bright and quite modern.

spans.value: The first sentence gives Sara new information. The next two sentences identify and describe something now established in the conversation.

sections.title: Transfer to a new situation: a neighbourhood visit

spans.value: The next day, Sara and Jonas visit Jonas’s friend Emil, who has recently moved to a new neighbourhood. The setting changes, but the same meaning choice remains useful.
Emil might introduce the area like this:

no.value: Det finnes en matbutikk rett rundt hjørnet.

en.value: There is a grocery shop just around the corner.

no.value: Det finnes også et bibliotek i nærheten.

en.value: There is also a library nearby.

spans.value: When Sara sees a building and asks about it, Emil identifies it:

no.value: Det er biblioteket.

en.value: That is the library.

spans.value: He can then describe it:

no.value: Det er nytt og veldig lyst.

en.value: It is new and very bright.

spans.value: If Jonas asks about transport, he asks whether a service exists:

no.value: Finnes det en buss til sentrum?

en.value: Is there a bus to the town centre?

spans.value: Emil can confirm its existence and then identify the stop:

no.value: Ja, det finnes en buss hvert tiende minutt.

en.value: Yes, there is a bus every ten minutes.

no.value: Det er holdeplassen på den andre siden av gata.

en.value: It is the stop on the other side of the street.

prompt.value: Choose the explanation that fits all three messages.

options.text: The first line asks whether a room exists; the second names a specific luggage room; the third says a restaurant is available.
options.why: The first line is a statement rather than a question, the second announces the luggage room rather than naming it, and the third asks about the restaurant rather than announcing it.

options.text: The first line names a specific room; the second says a luggage room is available; the third asks whether a restaurant exists.
options.why: Det er rom 214 names a particular room, det finnes et bagasjerom announces something available, and finnes det en restaurant? asks whether it exists.

options.text: The first line says a room is available; the second names a specific luggage room; the third asks whether a restaurant exists.
options.why: The first two jobs are swapped: the opening line names room 214, while the luggage-room line announces availability.

explanation.value: Når noe allerede er nevnt, beskriver eller lokaliserer vi det i stedet for å presentere det som noe nytt.

spans.value: Gjesten: Hvordan er rom 214? Ingrid:
ganske lyst og stille. Gjesten: Hvor er nøkkelkortet? Ingrid:
på rommet. Gjesten: Hvilket rom er dette? Ingrid:
rommet ved heisen.

prompt.value: Choose the question that asks whether the hotel has a café.

options.text: Finnes det en kafé på hotellet?
options.why: The guest asks whether a café exists at the hotel, so the question is about availability.
This asks whether a particular, already-known café is open; it does not ask whether one exists.

text.value: «Jeg har ikke vært på hotellet før. Hva kan jeg spise der?»

prompt.value: Complete the messages. Use «det finnes» when Ingrid tells Sara about a new place, and «det er» when she talks about a place already mentioned.

explanation.value: «Det finnes» presenterer et sted som ny informasjon. «Det er» brukes til å identifisere eller beskrive et sted som allerede er nevnt.

spans.value: Sara: Er det en kafé ved torget? Ingrid:
en kafé ved torget. Sara: Hvilken bygning er kafeen? Ingrid:
den røde bygningen ved torget. Jonas: Er det et apotek ved busstasjonen? Ingrid:
et apotek ved busstasjonen. Jonas: Hvilken bygning er apoteket? Ingrid:
den gule bygningen ved busstasjonen.

prompt.value: Ingrid is talking about a luggage room they already know about. Choose the phrase that does not fit.

payload.feedback: Replace «finnes» with «er»: the already-known luggage room is being described, not introduced as existing.

explanation.value: Den første replikken beskriver et rom som allerede er nevnt. I den siste replikken presenterer Ingrid et nytt tilbud med «det finnes». I dagligtale kan «det er» også brukes om noe som finnes.

prompt.value: Write a message to Sara. Tell her there is a laundry room, then use «det er» and a fact about the room or door to show where it is.

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate only the visible message task. Criteria availability-form, follow-up-forms are gating; no criterion is diagnostic-only. Valid variant that must pass: «Det finnes et vaskerom i andre etasje. Det er rommet med det blå skiltet ved trappa.» Near-miss that must fail because it never uses det finnes: «Vaskerommet er i andre etasje.» Near-miss that must fail because it never identifies or describes the laundry room with det er: «Det finnes et vaskerom i andre etasje.»

criteria.instruction: The message announces the laundry room as available using det finnes.
The message then uses det er to identify or describe the laundry room with at least one supplied detail that helps Sara find it.

prompt.value: Write a message to a visiting friend. A free information leaflet in Norwegian is in the blue basket at the far right of the entrance. Use «det finnes» for the leaflet and «det er» to point out the basket.

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate only the visible message task. Criteria guide-facts, availability-form, basket-identification are gating; no criterion is diagnostic-only. Valid variant that must pass: «Det finnes en gratis informasjonsbrosjyre på norsk. Den ligger i en blå kurv ved inngangen. Det er kurven lengst til høyre.» Near-miss that must fail because it omits the brochure's availability: «Brosjyren ligger i en blå kurv ved inngangen.» Near-miss that must fail because it does not identify the correct basket with det er: «Det finnes en gratis informasjonsbrosjyre på norsk, og kurvene står ved inngangen.»

criteria.instruction: The message accurately mentions a free Norwegian information brochure and that it is in the rightmost blue basket by the entrance.
The message presents the information brochure as available using det finnes.
The message uses det er to identify which basket contains the guide, with a supplied detail.

prompt.value: Reply to Sara. Outside the hotel there is a red bicycle that guests can borrow. Say that the bicycle is available, then use «det er» to say which bicycle you mean.

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate only the visible reply task. Criteria retrieval-facts, retrieval-forms are gating; no criterion is diagnostic-only. Valid variant that must pass: «Det finnes en sykkel du kan låne. Det er den røde sykkelen utenfor hotellet.» Near-miss that must fail because it produces neither target form: «Du kan låne den røde sykkelen utenfor hotellet.» Near-miss that must fail because it omits which bicycle it is: «Det finnes en sykkel du kan låne.»

criteria.instruction: The reply accurately states that the hotel has a bicycle available to borrow and identifies it as the red bicycle outside the hotel.
The reply uses det finnes to present the available bicycle and det er to identify which bicycle it is.

prompt.value: Choose the reply that first introduces the coat room as new information, then says where it is.

options.text: Ja, det finnes en gratis garderobe ved inngangen.
options.why: «Det finnes» introduces the not-yet-mentioned service as available, and the rest tells where it is.

options.text: Ja, den gratis garderoben er ved inngangen.
options.why: This locates an already identified cloakroom instead of introducing the service as newly available.

text.value: «Kan jeg henge fra meg jakken gratis her?»

options.text: Finnes det en buss som går fra stasjonen til sentrum?
options.why: Jonas asks whether a bus service exists for that route, not where a known bus is parked.
This asks where an already-known bus is; it does not ask whether a bus service is available.

text.value: «Jeg vet ikke om det går buss fra stasjonen til sentrum.»

prompt.value: The guests already know about the luggage room. Choose the reply that uses «det er» to say where it is.

options.why: This identifies what the thing is instead of answering where it is.

options.text: Det finnes et bagasjerom ved resepsjonen.
options.why: This mentions available storage but does not locate the known bagasjerom.
Det er with a place phrase locates a room that is already established in the conversation.
This describes the room but does not say where it is.

text.value: «Jeg har hørt at hotellet har et bagasjerom. Hvor ligger det?»
